guidance: Transmitter and bench aid for double-sideband AM with a steady carrier. Peak envelope power is the figure a PA and most regulators are rated by; keep the depth at or below 100 % unless the modulator is deliberately overdriven, and confirm wattmeter readings against a calibrated instrument.
method: AM keeps the carrier at its unmodulated power and splits the message into two sidebands, one either side of it, so a single tone at fm produces lines at fc - fm and fc + fm and occupies 2 x fm. With carrier power Pc and modulation index m (the audio peak divided by the unmodulated carrier peak, entered as a percentage), each sideband carries Pc.m^2/4, so the pair carries Pc.m^2/2 and the total power is Pc.(1 + m^2/2). A 100 W carrier at 50 % therefore rises to 112.5 W, of which 12.5 W is sideband and 100 W is carrier that carries no information; at 100 % the carrier is twice the sideband power, and the sideband share of the total - the efficiency m^2/(2 + m^2) - is then 33.3 %, up from 11.1 % at 50 %. Peak envelope power is the power at the crest of the envelope: the envelope peaks at (1 + m) times the carrier, so PEP = Pc.(1 + m)^2, which is four times the carrier at 100 % depth and is why an AM transmitter is rated by PEP rather than by carrier. Each sideband line stands at m/2 of the carrier amplitude, so a spectrum analyser showing sidebands 25 % of the carrier height each means 50 % depth. A standard envelope modulator cannot exceed 100 %: the trough reaches zero at full modulation, and beyond that the negative peaks are clipped, so depths above 100 % are computed and flagged as overmodulation instead of being refused, and the power values stay those of the linear model. If a measured total power is supplied, the depth it implies is sqrt(2.(Pt/Pc - 1)) and is reported beside the entered depth with the difference in percentage points; a measured total below the carrier is refused because amplitude modulation can only add sideband power. The rise over the unmodulated carrier is 10.log10(1 + m^2/2). Carrier power accepts 0.001 to 1,000,000 W, depth 0 to 200 %, modulating frequency 0.001 to 100,000 kHz and measured total power 0.001 to 1,000,000 W, in ordinary decimal notation only; a missing, non-numeric or out-of-range value is rejected with an actionable message rather than defaulted. A single steady sinusoidal tone, a linear modulator and a constant carrier are assumed; speech crest factor, compression, ALC, suppressed-carrier DSB, SSB, vestigial sideband and the occupancy rules of any particular broadcast service are not modelled. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Amplitude modulation: the modulation index is the audio peak divided by the unmodulated carrier amplitude, and at 100 % sine modulation the carrier power is twice the total sideband power
Peak envelope power: at 100 % symmetrical AM the peak envelope power is four times the carrier power, so an AM transmitter is rated at about a quarter of its PEP in carrier
